info.title: RoyalTechno AI API
info.description:
**RoyalTechno AI** is an async REST API for generating **videos and images** from
text or reference images. A single endpoint covers every supported model — the
live list is in the tables below and in `GET /v1/pricing` — so you can switch
quality and cost tiers without rewriting client code. Credit-metered.

Writing a client, or letting an AI agent write one? Read **Rules for scripts
and AI agents** below first — every limit there is enforced, and the reference
client at https://royaltechno.ai/api-docs#rules already follows them.

## Quick start

Get an API key from our Telegram bot
([@royaltechno_ai_bot](https://t.me/royaltechno_ai_bot)) — send `/api_key`;
registration is open. Every generation is a single POST. **Video:**

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.royaltechno.cc/v1/jobs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rt_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "model": "veo-3.1",
        "input": {
          "prompt": "A serene mountain landscape at sunrise, gentle camera pan",
          "aspect_ratio": "landscape",
          "duration_sec": 8
        }
      }'
```

**Text-to-image** works the same way — just pick an image model:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.royaltechno.cc/v1/jobs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rt_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "model": "nano-banana-pro",
        "input": {
          "prompt": "A royal crown made of glass, studio lighting",
          "aspect_ratio": "landscape"
        }
      }'
```

**Animate an image you generated here** — the `output.url` of a finished image job is a
permanent public URL, so feed it straight back in as `start_image_url`. No download,
no re-hosting, no base64:

```bash
# 1) the image job above finished → its output.url is:
#    https://cdn.royaltechno.cc/saas/images/job_xR3mK9pQvL2w.png
curl -X POST https://api.royaltechno.cc/v1/jobs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rt_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "model": "veo-3.1",
        "input": {
          "prompt": "The crown slowly rotates, light glinting across the glass",
          "start_image_url": "https://cdn.royaltechno.cc/saas/images/job_xR3mK9pQvL2w.png"
        }
      }'
```

Any image model can feed any video model this way, and the source image does not have to
come from us — see **Image inputs** below for the full rules, including first+last-frame
interpolation (send a second image as `end_image_url` and Veo or Seedance 2.0 animates
the transition).

The response returns `201` immediately with an `id`. Poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` —
every **10 s for video, 5 s for images**, sending the last
`ETag` back as `If-None-Match` (a `304` means nothing changed) — until `status` is
`succeeded` (with `output.url` set) or `failed` (with `error.message`):

```bash
curl https://api.royaltechno.cc/v1/jobs/job_xR3... \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rt_live_..." \
  -H 'If-None-Match: "<etag from the previous 200>"'
```

Images typically complete in well under a minute; video takes **minutes, not
seconds** (during busy periods, tens of minutes — the `queue_position` field on
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}` shows where you stand). Never resubmit a job because it
seems slow: you'd pay twice for the same clip.

Delivered `output.url` links are **stable public URLs** — no signature or expiry
timestamp in the link, safe to hotlink. They stay live while the files are
retained (no retention window is currently configured; if one ever applies,
jobs past it report `media_expired: true` instead of serving a dead link) —
download anything you must keep long-term.

## Rules for scripts and AI agents

Every limit below is enforced. A client that follows these ten rules never sees
a `429`, and a client that ignores them is slowed, then blocked. If you are an
AI agent writing a client: implement every rule; the reference client at
https://royaltechno.ai/api-docs#rules already does.

1. **Poll, don't hammer.** Poll `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` every **10 s for
   video** and **5 s for images**, `GET /v1/chains/{id}` every
   **30 s**. Always send `If-None-Match: <ETag from the last 200>`;
   a `304` means nothing changed — keep the same interval. Never poll faster than
   every 5 s, and poll all your jobs from ONE loop, not a thread per job.
2. **Keep at most 20 jobs in flight per API key** (`queued` +
   `processing`), submitting the next one when one finishes. Generation runs at
   your plan's concurrency per family (3–10 by plan, 10 for
   wallet-funded jobs), up to ×4 of that while the fleet is idle, and
   never more than 20 per key — so anything beyond
   20 only sits in `queued` (cap 100), burns queue slots
   and poll budget, and finishes no sooner. `GET /v1/account` →
   `limits.recommended_max_in_flight` is YOUR number, live.
3. **Never resubmit a job that is `queued` or `processing`.** Slow is not
   failed — video takes minutes, tens of minutes at peak (`queue_position`
   shows where you stand). Resubmitting doubles your spend and the load.
4. **On any `429`: sleep `Retry-After` seconds, then retry the same request
   once**, with the same `Idempotency-Key`; on repeats back off exponentially
   (`wait = max(Retry-After, min(60, 2^attempt) ± 20 % jitter)`) and
   give up after 6 attempts. On `429 queue_full` do not retry the
   POST at all: keep polling the jobs you have and submit again after one
   completes (`Retry-After` is 60 s; the endpoint answers
   `queue_full` cheaply for the next 15 s). Ignoring
   `Retry-After` gains nothing: refused calls are slowed to ~2 s each,
   30 refusals in a minute pause that endpoint for 120 s,
   and a client that keeps flooding is blocked with `403 access_banned` for
   6 hours.
5. **Stop on `400`, `401`, `402`, `403`.** They never clear by retrying: fix
   the request, the key, the balance or plan, or wait out the ban. Their
   `Retry-After` is information, not an invitation to loop.
6. **Only `503` is worth an automatic retry** (same backoff, same
   `Idempotency-Key`); for `model_unavailable` watch `GET /v1/status` and
   resubmit when the model is back.
7. **One `Idempotency-Key` (UUID v4) per distinct job**, generated once and
   reused only for retries of that exact request. The key identifies the
   request for 24 h: a **different body under a reused key returns
   the first job's response unchanged, without an error**.
8. **Budget:** an obedient client sends well under 1 request/s per key. The
   ceiling is 25 req/s (bursts to 100) per key and
   50 req/s (bursts to 200) per IP — hitting it means the
   client is wrong, not that it needs a bigger allowance.
9. **There is no bulk endpoint.** `POST /v1/jobs` takes one job (`input.count`
   ≤ 4 variants of one prompt); `POST /v1/chains` is a serial movie, not a
   batch. Loop with the sliding window above.
10. **Machine-readable copies:** https://api.royaltechno.cc/llms.txt (plain text) and
    `info.x-client-rules` in https://api.royaltechno.cc/openapi.json. Reference client (Python /
    Node): https://royaltechno.ai/api-docs#rules.


## Authentication

Every request except `/health` needs a Bearer token:

```http
Authorization: Bearer rt_live_<random32>
```

Keys never appear in our database in plain form — only the SHA-256 hash. The full
key is shown to you **once** at creation and cannot be recovered. If you suspect a
key was leaked, issue a new one immediately; the old one returns `401`.

## Supported models

Pass any of these as `model` on `POST /v1/jobs`. Names follow our upstream
(useapi) conventions. This list is generated from the live catalog, so it
always matches what's actually orderable — the cost matrix at `GET /v1/pricing`
carries the authoritative per-model numbers.

### Video

| Model | Name | Price | Default duration |
|---|---|---|---|
| `veo-3.1` | Veo 3.1 1080p | $0.05 | 8s |
| `omni-flash` | Gemini Omni Flash | $0.01/s | 8s |
| `seedance-2.0-mini` | Seedance 2.0 Mini | $0.08/s | 5s |
| `seedance-2.0-fast` | Seedance 2.0 Fast | $0.09/s | 5s |
| `seedance-2.0` | Seedance 2.0 | $0.11/s | 5s |

### Image

| Model | Name | Price (per image) |
|---|---|---|
| `nano-banana-pro` | Nano Banana Pro | $0.02 |
| `nano-banana-2` | Nano Banana 2 | $0.02 |
| `seedream-4.6` | Seedream 4.6 | $0.03 |
| `gpt-image-2` | GPT Image 2 | $0.04 |

- **Duration** (video): per-second models accept any `duration_sec` from 2 to 15 and bill the exact length — `seedance-2.0` at `7` costs 7 × the per-second rate. The durations listed in `GET /v1/pricing` are a convenience shortlist, not a limit. A few models are restricted to a fixed set by their provider (`omni-flash`: 4/6/8/10) and reject anything else with `400 invalid_value` before any charge. Fixed-duration models (e.g. Veo at 8s) charge per clip and ignore `duration_sec`. Aspect: `landscape` (16:9) or `portrait` (9:16).
- **Resolution**: most video is 720p; `veo-3.1` and `seedance-2.0` also accept `"resolution": "1080p"` (priced higher — see `GET /v1/pricing`). High-res **image** variants are selected the same way rather than by a separate model name: `nano-banana-pro` and `nano-banana-2` accept `"2k"` and `"4k"` (metered at 2x / 4x credit weight on quota plans), `gpt-image-2` accepts `"4k"`. Values a model can't serve are rejected with `400 unsupported_resolution`. Omit the field (or send `"auto"`) for the model default — every row in `GET /v1/pricing` is copy-paste-able. If an upstream upscale is temporarily unavailable, a job may be delivered at a lower resolution than ordered; that is always flagged by the `notice` object on the job (see **Degraded delivery**), never done silently.
- **Image input**: every video model accepts `start_image_url` (image-to-video) — including a URL we returned from an image job, so you can generate a frame here and animate it in the next call. Veo and the Seedance 2.0 family additionally accept `end_image_url` for first+last-frame interpolation (`i2v_fl`). Image models with image-to-image support (Nano Banana Pro / Nano Banana 2, Seedream 4.6, GPT Image 2) also take `start_image_url` as the source to re-render; text-only image models reject it with `400 unsupported_combination`. All covered under **Image inputs** below.
- **Prompt length is per-model** (each model's real provider cap): `gpt-image-2` takes up to **32000** characters, `seedance-2.0` **5000**, most models **4000** (their providers publish no cap), and a few enforce less — `seedream-4.6` **1600**, the Kling family and Grok **2500**, `wan-2.6-flash` **1500**, Sora 2 and Gen-4 **1000**. Over-cap prompts are rejected with `400 prompt_too_long` **before any charge**, and the message names your length and the model's cap.

## Image inputs (image-to-video & first+last frame)

Every video model takes a source image. Pass `start_image_url` and the clip starts from
that frame (mode `i2v`) instead of from text alone.

`start_image_url` (and optional `end_image_url`) accept **three** kinds of value:

| Value | Example | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| A URL **we** returned | `"https://cdn.royaltechno.cc/saas/images/job_xR3....png"` | **Chaining** — animate an image you generated here |
| Any HTTPS URL | `"https://example.com/photo.jpg"` | Image already publicly hosted |
| Inline data URI | `"data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQ..."` | Local files — no separate hosting needed |

- **Chaining is the common case:** generate with an image model, poll until `succeeded`,
  then pass that job's `output.url` as the next job's `start_image_url`. Those URLs are
  public and stable, so nothing has to be downloaded, re-hosted or base64-encoded in
  between. Nothing marks a "generated" image as special — it is just a URL we can fetch.
- Inline data URIs are decoded server-side and stored in R2 for the worker.
- **Limit:** 5 MiB decoded. **Accepted mime:** `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/webp`.
- **`aspect_ratio` is ignored** whenever `start_image_url` is set: an i2v clip inherits the
  source image's shape. To get a 9:16 clip, generate (or supply) a 9:16 source image.
- **Multi-reference** (`reference_image_urls`): pass an array of conditioning images to composite/condition on more than one input. Image models **Nano Banana Pro / Nano Banana 2** accept up to **10** and **Seedream 4.6** up to **6** (compose a subject into a scene); video models **Seedance 2.0** up to 9, **Gemini Omni Flash** up to 7, and **Veo 3.1** up to 3 ("ingredients" — e.g. characters + a location, reference-to-video). Same formats/limits as `start_image_url`; mutually exclusive with `start_image_url`/`end_image_url` and `count` > 1.

### First + last frame (`i2v_fl`)

Send **two** images — `start_image_url` and `end_image_url` — and the model animates the
transition between them: the first is the opening frame, the second is the frame you want
to end on. Supported on **Veo** (`veo-3.1`) and the **Seedance 2.0 family**
(`seedance-2.0*`); any other model returns
`400 unsupported_combination`, and `end_image_url` without `start_image_url` is rejected.

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.royaltechno.cc/v1/jobs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer rt_live_..." \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
        "model": "veo-3.1",
        "input": {
          "prompt": "The camera pushes in as the crown settles into place",
          "start_image_url": "https://cdn.royaltechno.cc/saas/images/job_xR3mK9pQvL2w.png",
          "end_image_url": "data:image/jpeg;base64,/9j/4AAQSkZJRgABA..."
        }
      }'
```

Both slots take any of the three value kinds above — mix a generated first frame with an
uploaded last frame if that is what you have.

## Rate limits

Current defaults (per API key unless stated; `GET /v1/account` → `limits`
returns the live numbers for YOUR key):

| Limit | Default | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Requests per API key | 25/s sustained, bursts to 100 | `429 too_many_requests`, refused before authentication; `Retry-After` = seconds to the next slot. Heavier integrations can ask for a per-key allowance |
| Requests per client IP | 50/s sustained, bursts to 200 | same code — several keys behind one NAT share it |
| Queue depth per API key | 100 jobs in `queued` + `processing` | `429 queue_full` past this, with a `Retry-After: 60` header. For ~15 s after that refusal the same endpoint answers `429 queue_full` without re-checking the queue (`Retry-After` = seconds left); status polling is unaffected |
| Concurrent generation | your plan's concurrency per family (3–10 by plan, 10 for wallet-funded jobs), up to ×4 while the fleet is idle, never more than 20 per key | Jobs beyond that wait in `queued` — more in flight never finishes sooner. Keep ≤ 20 in flight |
| Rejected requests per key | 30 per minute, **per endpoint** | `429 too_many_failed_requests` — that endpoint is paused for 120 s for the key, with `Retry-After`; other endpoints keep working |
| Idempotency-Key TTL | 24 hours | Same key returns the cached response — even for a different body |

Pass `Idempotency-Key: <your-uuid>` on `POST /v1/jobs` to make submits safely retriable.

> 💡 **Successful** throughput is not rate limited — but pace submissions with
> a sliding window: keep at most 20 jobs in flight per key and
> submit the next one when one finishes. Jobs beyond that only wait in the
> queue; they do not finish sooner, and every queued job costs you a poll.
>
> ⚠️ **Rejections are.** If we refuse your requests (`401`, `402`, `403`,
> `429`) and your client retries in a tight loop, that endpoint is paused for
> 120 s with `429 too_many_failed_requests`. Budgets are per
> endpoint: failing `POST /v1/jobs` while `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` succeeds still
> pauses the POST. A `429 queue_full` additionally pauses submits on the spot
> for ~15 s — one strike, no loop needed — and the paused endpoint answers
> slowly on purpose (~2 s per call), so a client that ignores `Retry-After`
> gains nothing by retrying. There is also an absolute ceiling per key and per
> IP (table above): a client that keeps ignoring it is slowed and, if it
> keeps going, blocked (`403 access_banned`, 6 h). Refusals like `plan_expired` and
> `insufficient_credits` will not clear by retrying — they need a top-up or
> renewal. Always honour `Retry-After`; a `503` is the only refusal worth
> retrying automatically (use the same `Idempotency-Key`).

## Video chains

`POST /v1/chains` renders an ordered prompt list as ONE continuous movie: each
~8s clip natively continues the previous one (real motion continuity — no
last-frame splicing on your side), the finished movie is assembled losslessly
and finished at **1080p for free**. Clips generate at native 720p by design —
that is what keeps long chains artifact-free.

Chains run strictly serially (~2–4 min per clip; a 10-clip chain is a
30–60 minute job) and charge **per clip when its turn starts** — nothing at
create, no charge for clips that never run. Runs out of balance mid-chain →
the chain pauses and auto-resumes after a top-up. Poll `GET /v1/chains/{id}`
every 30 s for per-clip progress and the final `stitch.url`;
`POST /v1/chains/{id}/cancel` stops the un-started remainder.

## Errors

Every non-2xx response uses a Stripe-shaped envelope. `error.type` is the coarse
category to switch on (`invalid_request`, `authentication_error`,
`rate_limit_exceeded`, …); `error.code` is the precise machine-readable cause:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request",
    "code": "invalid_value",
    "message": "Unknown model 'veo-99'.",
    "param": "model",
    "request_id": "req_..."
  }
}
```

| Code | HTTP | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| `invalid_image` | 400 | Image input is malformed or not a decodable image. |
| `invalid_value` | 400 | Field validation failed — `param` names the field, the message explains. |
| `invalid_video` | 400 | `reference_video_url` is malformed, not an https:// MP4 URL, or not one of your uploads. |
| `missing_param` | 400 | A required field is absent — `param` names it. |
| `prompt_empty` | 400 | Prompt is empty or whitespace-only. |
| `prompt_too_long` | 400 | Prompt exceeds this model's character cap (`prompt_max` on the model entry) — the message names both numbers. |
| `route_not_permitted` | 400 | `input.route` is reserved for internal service callers. |
| `source_video_too_long` | 400 | Source clip exceeds the 10 s video-editing limit — trim the file before uploading. |
| `start_image_required` | 400 | Model is image-to-video only — provide `input.start_image_url`. |
| `too_many_prompts` | 400 | Chain `prompts` exceeds the live per-chain cap — the message states it. |
| `too_many_reference_images` | 400 | More reference images than this model's cap (see the model table). |
| `unpriced_model` | 400 | No price exists for this parameter combination — treat as unsupported. |
| `unsupported_combination` | 400 | Fields that cannot be combined (e.g. `end_image_url` on a model without first+last-frame support, or `reference_image_urls` together with `start_image_url`). |
| `unsupported_count` | 400 | `count` > 1 on a model that generates one output per request. |
| `unsupported_image_type` | 400 | Image mime type is not jpeg/png/webp. |
| `unsupported_reference_input` | 400 | `reference_image_urls` on a model without reference support. |
| `unsupported_resolution` | 400 | `resolution` is not on this model's menu — the message lists valid values. |
| `unsupported_video_input` | 400 | `reference_video_url` on a model without video-to-video support. |
| `upscale_not_eligible` | 400 | Source job cannot be upscaled (internal endpoint). |
| `video_trim_required` | 400 | `trim_start_sec`/`trim_end_sec` are required for an https:// source — its length can't be measured before charging. |
| `invalid_credentials` | 401 | API key is invalid or was revoked. |
| `missing_credentials` | 401 | No `Authorization` header. Format: `Bearer rt_live_…`. |
| `daily_limit_reached` | 402 | Your plan's daily quota can't cover this request and your balance can't cover the pay-as-you-go price — wait for the reset (`error.data.reset_at`, 00:00 Europe/Kyiv) or top up via the bot. Carries `Retry-After`. |
| `insufficient_credits` | 402 | Balance below the job cost — top up via the bot. |
| `model_not_in_plan` | 402 | You hold an active plan, but it does not cover this model — the model is pay-as-you-go and your balance can't cover its price. `error.data.active_plans` lists your plans; top up via the bot or pick a covered model from `GET /v1/pricing`. Carries `Retry-After`. |
| `plan_expired` | 402 | Your plan expired and your balance can't cover the pay-as-you-go price — renew the plan or top up via the bot. `error.data.plan_id` names the lapsed plan. Retrying will NOT succeed until you act; honour `Retry-After`. |
| `access_banned` | 403 | This API key or network address is temporarily blocked after sustained abusive request rates (auto-bans last 6 h). It lifts automatically — `Retry-After` is the remaining time — or sooner via support in the bot. Retrying does not shorten it. |
| `account_suspended` | 403 | Account suspended for abuse — contact support via the bot. |
| `account_under_review` | 403 | Account is under a security review — contact support via the bot. |
| `upscale_not_permitted` | 403 | Upscale is internal-only; public keys always get this. |
| `not_found` | 404 | No such job id under this API key. |
| `chain_not_active` | 409 | The chain has already finished — pause/resume no longer applies. |
| `pinned_provider_unavailable` | 409 | Internal callers only: the pinned provider cannot serve this model. |
| `image_too_large` | 413 | Decoded inline image exceeds 5 MiB — host it and pass an https:// URL. |
| `request_too_large` | 413 | Request body exceeds the transport cap — use https:// image URLs instead of inline base64. |
| `chain_limit_reached` | 429 | You already have the maximum number of active chains — wait or cancel one. `error.data.active_chain_ids` lists the chains holding the slots (cancel via `POST /v1/chains/{id}/cancel`). Carries `Retry-After`; the same short cheap backoff as `queue_full` applies. |
| `queue_full` | 429 | Your queue is at its cap (100 jobs queued + processing). Do NOT resubmit and do not retry the POST: keep polling the jobs you already have and submit again after one finishes; the response carries `Retry-After` (60 s). After the first refusal the same endpoint answers this code cheaply for up to ~15 s without re-checking the queue (`Retry-After` = seconds left); status polling is unaffected. |
| `too_many_failed_requests` | 429 | More than 30 of your requests to one endpoint were rejected within a minute (expired plan, exhausted quota, or a bad key), so that endpoint is paused for 120 s for this key — other endpoints, e.g. status polling, keep working. Fix the cause and honour `Retry-After` — retrying sooner just extends the pause. |
| `too_many_requests` | 429 | Request-rate ceiling for this API key or client IP (default 25/s sustained, bursts to 100 per key; 50/s, bursts to 200 per IP). Answered before authentication; `Retry-After` is the seconds until the next slot. Poll with backoff, not in a tight loop — a client that keeps ignoring the ceiling is slowed, then blocked. Heavier integrations can ask for a per-key allowance. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | Unexpected server error — quote the `request_id` to support. |
| `chains_disabled` | 503 | Video chains are temporarily disabled — retry later. |
| `model_unavailable` | 503 | Model temporarily out of supply — do NOT tight-retry; watch `GET /v1/status` and resubmit when it recovers. |
| `storage_unavailable` | 503 | Transient storage failure while persisting an inline image — safe to retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`. |

Include the `request_id` in any support ping — it's our log correlation key.

### Job failures

An API-layer error above means the request never became a job. A job that was
accepted but failed during generation comes back as `status: "failed"` with an
`error` object (`type` is always `upstream_error` there) and one of these
`error.code` values:

| Code | Retryable | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `content_policy` | see `error.retryable` | The provider's content filter rejected the request. Prompt/image verdicts are deterministic (`retryable: false`) — edit before resubmitting; identical resubmits are rejected instantly for a repeat window. Audio-track verdicts (the message names the audio safety filter) are sampling-dependent (`retryable: true`) — one automatic retry was already made, and resubmitting the same request often succeeds |
| `invalid_input` | no | Input the provider can't process (e.g. prompt too long for this model) |
| `rate_limited` | yes | Provider temporarily overloaded |
| `timeout` | yes | Generation or delivery timed out on our side |
| `provider_error` | yes | Generic upstream failure |
| `internal_error` | yes | Failure inside our pipeline |

`retryable: false` means resubmitting the same request will fail again — change
it first. `retryable: true` on a `content_policy` failure marks a
sampling-dependent verdict (the audio safety filter): the identical request
often passes on resubmit. Failed jobs are **auto-refunded**; you never pay for
a failed generation.

### Degraded delivery

A job can also *succeed* while delivering less than what was ordered — most
often when an upstream upscale stage is temporarily down and a 1080p clip comes
back at 720p. Those jobs are `status: "succeeded"` with usable `output`, plus a
`notice` object:

```json
{
  "status": "succeeded",
  "input": { "resolution": "1080p" },
  "notice": {
    "code": "resolution_downgraded",
    "message": "1080p is temporarily unavailable due to a supplier defect — this video was generated in 720p.",
    "requested_resolution": "1080p",
    "delivered_resolution": "720p"
  }
}
```

`notice` is `null` on every job delivered as ordered. Switch on `notice.code`
(stable); `notice.message` is English prose and may be reworded. `input`
always echoes what you **ordered**, so compare it against
`notice.delivered_resolution` to see the substitution. Degraded jobs on a
pay-as-you-go balance or a free allowance are **refunded in full**; plan-funded
jobs are not re-billed. Retrying immediately usually reproduces the same
downgrade — the condition is upstream and clears on its own.

## Pricing

Pricing is **per-second** for video (per clip for fixed-duration models) and
**flat per generation** for image. Your balance must cover the cost *before*
submit or you'll get `402 insufficient_credits` — or `402 daily_limit_reached`
when a plan's daily quota is what ran out (`error.data.reset_at` says when it
resets; daily quotas reset at 00:00 Europe/Kyiv).

Get the live matrix from `GET /v1/pricing`. Top up self-service in the bot
(crypto via @CryptoBot or Binance Pay, or a subscription plan via `/plans`).

post.description:
Create a new generation job.

Async — returns immediately with a job id (status=`queued`); poll
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}` until terminal (`succeeded` / `failed` / `canceled`).
Cost is debited from your balance at submit time and refunded if the
job fails.

**Body shape:** see the schema below. The `model` field selects the
backend — the live list of orderable names (video AND image) is in the
"Supported models" tables above and in `GET /v1/pricing`. High-res image
variants are selected via `input.resolution` rather than a separate model
name: `nano-banana-pro` or `nano-banana-2` with `resolution: "2k"` or
`"4k"` returns the premium high-res output (priced higher; metered at
2x / 4x credit weight on quota plans), and `gpt-image-2` accepts `"4k"` —
see the `input.resolution` schema for the full per-model menu. The
`input.start_image_url` accepts either an HTTPS URL
or an inline `data:image/...;base64,...` URI (≤ 5 MiB decoded).

**Image-to-video, including your own generations:** pass
`input.start_image_url` to any video model and the clip starts from that
frame. A finished image job's `output.url` can be used verbatim — those
URLs are public and stable (see `media_expired` for retention), so
generating an image here and animating it is two calls with nothing in
between. Veo (`veo-3.1`) and the Seedance 2.0 family (`seedance-2.0*`)
also accept `input.end_image_url` (first + last frame: the model animates
the transition between the two images); other models reject it with
`400 unsupported_combination`.

**Idempotency:** pass `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` header to make the
request safely retriable. Same key within 24h returns the cached
response without creating a new job.

**Errors:** see the "Errors" table in the introduction above — it lists
every `error.code` with its HTTP status and how to react. Failed jobs
(accepted, then failed during generation) are documented under
"Job failures" there; they auto-refund.

get.description:
Fetch a job by its `external_id`.

Poll this endpoint to watch status transitions:
`queued` → `processing` → `succeeded` (with `output.url`) or `failed`
(with `error.message`). Generation itself typically takes 1–5 minutes
once dispatched, but **queue wait varies with load** — during peak hours
a job can stay `queued` for tens of minutes. Use `queue_position` (set
while `status="queued"`) to track progress through the queue, keep your
client timeout generous (30+ min), and keep polling the SAME job id —
never resubmit a queued prompt, that doubles the load and your spend.

**Cadence:** poll every 10 s for video and 5 s for images, all your jobs
from one loop — see *Rules for scripts and AI agents* at the top of this
reference (`GET /v1/account` → `limits` has your live numbers).

**ETag support:** the response sets an `ETag` header. Pass it back as
`If-None-Match` on subsequent polls; identical state returns `304 Not
Modified` with no body — saves bandwidth when polling at high frequency.
Weak validators (`W/"…"`, what a CDN hands you when the response was
compressed) are accepted — echo the header exactly as you received it.
`queue_position` is excluded from the ETag: a `304` means status/output
unchanged — poll without `If-None-Match` when you want a fresh position.

**Errors:** `404 not_found` if no job with that id is owned by your API key.

429.description: Too Many Requests — `error.code` ∈ { queue_full · chain_limit_reached · too_many_failed_requests · too_many_requests }

post.description:
Cancel a job and refund its cost.

Idempotent — calling on an already-terminal job (`succeeded`/`failed`/
`canceled`) is a no-op and returns the current state. The refund only
fires the first time. Note: we mark the job canceled internally and
refund immediately; the backend may still complete the generation in
the background (best-effort cancellation upstream).

**Errors:** `404 not_found` if no job with that id is owned by your API key.

429.description: Too Many Requests — `error.code` ∈ { queue_full · chain_limit_reached · too_many_failed_requests · too_many_requests }

post.description:
Create a video chain — one continuous movie from an ordered prompt list.

Each ~8s clip natively CONTINUES the previous one (real motion
continuity, not last-frame splicing), so the scene flows across clips.
Clips render at native 720p — that is deliberate: it is what keeps long
chains artifact-free — and the finished movie is assembled losslessly
and finished at 1080p for free.

**Nothing is charged at create.** Each clip is charged individually when
its turn starts (so `402` never happens here); if the balance runs out
mid-chain the chain pauses (`status: "paused"`,
`pause_reason: "insufficient_credits"`) and resumes automatically after
a top-up. If the video fleet is momentarily at capacity the chain waits
(`pause_reason: "capacity"`) and resumes on its own — a capacity blip
never fails a chain. A clip that fails is retried once free of charge; if it fails
again the chain stops honestly — finished clips stay yours, unmade clips
are never charged.

Chains run strictly serially (~2-4 min per clip): a 10-clip chain is a
30-60 minute job. Poll `GET /v1/chains/{id}` for progress; each finished
clip's `clip_url` appears as it lands.

**Idempotency:** pass `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` to make the request
safely retriable (same semantics as POST /v1/jobs).

prompts: aerial view of an erupting volcano at dusk, photorealistic
the camera glides closer to the crater, lava fountains intensify
the camera pulls back revealing the full mountain at nightfall
the scene comes alive with gentle camera drift
the camera slowly circles the subject, cinematic

get.description:
Return the authenticated key's display info, credit balance, active
plans and live quota state.

The `balance_usd_cents` is the canonical integer (credit ledger sum).
`balance_usd` is the same value formatted as `$X.YY` for display.
The `key.prefix` + `key.last4` together identify the key without
exposing it; `key.label` is whatever the user set when minting.

Plan coverage (all four lists are empty on pay-as-you-go):

- `plans`: active subscriptions; `expires_at` is `null` for plans that
  never expire.
- `unlimited`: model kinds the plans cover without metering.
- `daily`: live daily-quota state per plan-covered kind. `limit` /
  `used_today` / `remaining_today` are **credits**, not generations —
  premium variants (2K/4K) burn more than one credit per generation.
  Quotas reset at 00:00 Europe/Kyiv; `reset_at` is that instant in UTC.
- `allowances`: metered credit buckets (plan grants, promo trial);
  `included` is `null` for non-plan grants.

`limits` is the **live pacing contract for this key** — the request
ceiling, queue cap, concurrency and the recommended poll cadence /
in-flight window. Configure your client from it rather than from the
docs' defaults; see *Rules for scripts and AI agents*.

Errors: `401 missing_credentials` / `401 invalid_credentials` if the
Authorization header is missing or the key is invalid/revoked.

get.description:
Return the full cost matrix in USD cents for every supported model.

One entry per (model, duration, resolution) combination. The model set and
every price are read straight from the live catalog (same source the bot's
confirm dialog uses), so this never drifts from what's orderable. Only
visible, in-supply models appear — mirroring the job-creation kill-switch
so customers never see a price they can't buy.

Just submit and read `cost_usd_cents` on the returned Job if you'd rather
not precompute — the API rejects with `402 insufficient_credits` if your
balance is below cost.

Output payload for a multi-image job.

Some image backends (notably the Seedream family) return multiple
images per generation by default. This shape surfaces all of them —
`images[0]` is the canonical/primary image (same one returned in the

JobImageOutput.description:
Output payload for a single-image job.

For jobs that produce exactly one image (`nano-banana-*`, `gpt-image-2`
and other single-output image models). Multi-image jobs use
`JobImageAlbumOutput` instead.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.description: Text prompt describing the video or image. The limit is PER-MODEL (each model's provider-side cap, served as `prompt_max`): `gpt-image-2` up to 32000, `seedance-2.0` 5000, most models 4000, and some enforce less — `seedream-4.6` 1600, Kling / Grok 2500, `wan-2.6-flash` 1500, Sora 2 / Gen-4 1000. Over the model's cap → `400 prompt_too_long` before any charge; the message names both numbers.

aspect_ratio.title: Aspect Ratio
aspect_ratio.description: Output aspect ratio. `landscape` = 16:9, `portrait` = 9:16. Honoured for text-to-video/image and for `reference_image_urls` jobs. **Ignored when you pass `start_image_url`** — an image-to-video job inherits the aspect ratio of that source image, so send a 9:16 source image to get a 9:16 clip. Note the ratio is a request field: writing "9:16" inside `prompt` text has no effect on the output frame.

duration_sec.title: Duration Sec
duration_sec.description: Video duration in seconds. Video models only; ignored for image models. Per-second models (e.g. Seedance) accept any value in range and bill the exact length — the durations shown in GET /v1/pricing are a shortlist, not a limit. A few models are restricted by their provider (omni-flash: 4/6/8/10) and reject anything else before any charge. Fixed-duration models (Veo, 8s per clip) ignore the value. Omit for the model default (8 for Veo, 5 for Seedance).

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: Audio (text-to-speech) models only: the voice id to speak with, from the model's `voices` list (GET /v1/web/models). Omit for the default voice. Ignored by video/image models.

language.title: Language
language.description: Audio models only: ISO 639-1 language of the text (`uk`, `ru`, `en`). Coerced onto the chosen voice's verified languages.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: Output resolution. Most video models are fixed at 720p; `veo-3.1` and `seedance-2.0` also support `1080p` (priced higher; for Veo it is a distinct tier, so a 1080p request never silently returns 720p). Images: `nano-banana-pro` and `nano-banana-2` accept `2k` and `4k` (premium high-res variants — priced higher and metered at 2x / 4x credit weight on quota plans; omit for standard ~1K); `gpt-image-2` accepts `4k` (true 3840x2160, 4x credit weight); `seedream-4.6` accepts `2k`. Values a model can't serve are rejected with `400 unsupported_resolution` — every `GET /v1/pricing` row is a valid value. Omit or send `auto` for the model's default.

start_image_url.title: Start Image Url
start_image_url.description: Source image for i2v / i2i. Either an HTTPS URL (`https://...`) or an inline data URI (`data:image/jpeg;base64,...`). Decoded data URIs are capped at 5 MiB. Allowed mime: image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp. **Chaining:** the `output.url` of a finished image job goes here as-is — those URLs are public and stable (see `media_expired` on the job for retention), so an image you generated with this API can be animated in the very next call with no download, re-hosting or base64 step.

end_image_url.title: End Image Url
end_image_url.description: Second image for first+last-frame interpolation (mode `i2v_fl`): `start_image_url` is the opening frame, this is the frame the clip ends on, and the model animates the transition between them. Supported on Veo video models (`veo-3.1`) and the Seedance 2.0 family (`seedance-2.0*`) — anything else returns `400 unsupported_combination`. Requires `start_image_url`. Same value formats as `start_image_url`, including a URL returned by a previous job.

reference_image_urls.title: Reference Image Urls
reference_image_urls.description: Reference images for multi-reference conditioning — e.g. a character sheet + a location plate (video) or a subject + a scene to composite (image). Supported on select models with a per-model cap: Nano Banana Pro / Nano Banana 2 up to 10 (image compositing), Seedream 4.6 up to 6 (image compositing), Seedance 2.0 up to 9, Gemini Omni Flash up to 7 (reference-to-video), Veo 3.1 up to 3 ('ingredients' reference-to-video). Each item is an HTTPS URL or an inline data URI, same format and limits as `start_image_url`. Mutually exclusive with `start_image_url`/`end_image_url` and with `count` > 1. Template-tool friendly: also accepts a single STRING — a JSON-encoded array (`"[\"https://a\", \"https://b\"]"`), comma- or newline-separated URLs (`"https://a, https://b"`), or one bare URL — coerced to the array form server-side.

reference_video_url.title: Reference Video Url
reference_video_url.description: Source clip for **video-to-video editing** — the model re-renders this footage following your prompt, keeping its motion and framing. Supported on `omni-flash` only. Must be an **HTTPS URL to an MP4** (inline base64 is not accepted for video — the request body limit makes it impractical). **The source clip must be 10 seconds or shorter**; longer sources are rejected. Pair it with `trim_start_sec`/`trim_end_sec` to edit part of a clip — the trimmed window becomes the output length and is what you are billed for, so `duration_sec` must be omitted. Mutually exclusive with `start_image_url`, `end_image_url`, `reference_image_urls`, and `count` > 1.

trim_start_sec.title: Trim Start Sec
trim_start_sec.description: Start of the edited window, in seconds from the beginning of `reference_video_url`. Defaults to 0. Required (together with `trim_end_sec`) when the source is an HTTPS URL, because we cannot know its length before charging you.

trim_end_sec.title: Trim End Sec
trim_end_sec.description: End of the edited window, in seconds. Must be greater than `trim_start_sec`, and the window must be at least 1 second. `trim_end_sec - trim_start_sec` is the output length **and** the billed duration.

count.title: Count
count.description: Number of variants to generate from this prompt in a single request (1-4). Supported on Google-backed models (Veo, Nano Banana, Gemini Omni Flash); other models generate one output per request and reject count > 1 with `unsupported_count`. Billed as N x the per-generation price; on a daily-quota plan the request costs N x the model's credit weight from today's quota (undelivered variants are automatically credited back). Multi-variant jobs return a `*_album` output.

route.title: Route
route.description: Internal-only: pin a specific provider route for this model (e.g. `runway` for a model whose default route is Dreamina). Rejected for normal API keys; honoured only for internal service callers.

JobInput.title: JobInput
JobInput.description:
Generation parameters. Field requirements depend on the chosen model
(provider + media_type derived in the router); validation lives there.

JobInputEcho.title: JobInputEcho
JobInputEcho.description:
The `input` block as echoed back on every Job response.

Mirrors what the customer submitted, normalized to the resolved
duration/resolution (after server-side defaults applied).

code.title: Code
code.description: Stable degrade token. `resolution_downgraded` = the requested resolution was temporarily unavailable upstream and the job was delivered at a lower one.

requested_resolution.title: Requested Resolution
requested_resolution.description: The resolution the job was submitted for.

JobNotice.title: JobNotice
JobNotice.description:
A non-fatal advisory about a job that SUCCEEDED but was delivered at
less than what was ordered.

Distinct from `error`, which only ever appears on `status="failed"`: a job
carrying a `notice` still produced usable output, it just isn't the full
thing the customer asked for. `code` is a stable machine token — switch on
it; `message` is human-readable English and may be reworded at any time.

output.title: Output
output.description: Set when `status="succeeded"`. The url is a public HTTPS URL — no signature or expiry timestamp in the link, safe to hotlink. It stays live while the files are retained (no retention window is currently configured; if one ever applies, jobs past it report `media_expired: true` with `output: null` — download anything you must keep long-term).

cost_usd_cents.title: Cost Usd Cents
cost_usd_cents.description: Cost debited at submit (refunded on failure).

media_expired.title: Media Expired
media_expired.description: `true` on a succeeded job whose generated files have passed the storage retention window and are no longer downloadable (`output` is `null` then). Absent while no retention window is configured, and on every job still inside it.

notice.description: Set on a SUCCEEDED job that was delivered below what was ordered — today only `resolution_downgraded`, when an upstream upscale is temporarily unavailable and the clip came back at a lower resolution. `null` on every job delivered as ordered. Cash and allowance jobs are refunded in full when this is set; plan-funded jobs are not re-billed.

queue_position.title: Queue Position
queue_position.description: Only while `status="queued"` (GET only): approximate 1-based position in the dispatch queue (your earlier jobs + other users' older queue-heads). Excluded from the ETag — a 304 means status/output unchanged; poll without If-None-Match for a fresh position.

JobResponse.title: JobResponse
JobResponse.description:
The canonical Job shape. Same on POST /v1/jobs (201), GET /v1/jobs/{id}
(200), and POST /v1/jobs/{id}/cancel (200).

input.prompt: A royal crown made of glass, studio lighting

self.title: Self
self.description: Absolute URL to GET this job.

cancel.title: Cancel
cancel.description: Absolute URL to POST to cancel this job.

JobUrls.title: JobUrls
JobUrls.description: Convenience HATEOAS links for the job. Saves clients string-concatenating.

videos.title: Videos
videos.description: At least 2 videos. Single-output responses use `JobVideoOutput` instead.

poster_url.title: Poster Url
poster_url.description: Poster frame (JPEG) of `videos[0]`, the primary variant. Absent while the poster is still being rendered.

JobVideoAlbumOutput.title: JobVideoAlbumOutput
JobVideoAlbumOutput.description:
Output payload for a multi-variant video job.

Flow models can generate 2-4 variants of one prompt in a single request
(`input.count`). This shape surfaces all of them — `videos[0]` is the
canonical/primary variant (same one a single-output job returns in the
`JobVideoOutput` shape) and the rest are additional variants.

url.title: Url
url.description: Permanent public HTTPS URL to the generated media.

JobVideoAlbumVideo.title: JobVideoAlbumVideo
JobVideoAlbumVideo.description: One video in a multi-variant album.

url.title: Url
url.description: Permanent public HTTPS URL to the generated media.

poster_url.title: Poster Url
poster_url.description: Permanent public HTTPS URL to a JPEG poster frame of the clip (first frame). Absent while the poster is still being rendered.

JobVideoOutput.title: JobVideoOutput
JobVideoOutput.description: Output payload for a successful video job.

ApiKey.description: Bearer token API key (`rt_live_...` or `rt_test_...`). Mint one via the Telegram bot's `/api_key_new` command.
